- `close` fit interval header line: The increment H(298.15)-H(0) is a derived value and unread; the exponent list is form structure declared in every interval (here always the standard set) and the fixed 7-term NASA9 form ignores it.
- `exact` fit coefficient lines: Units of the coefficients are dimensionless only with respect to R; the constants b1 and b2 carry the enthalpy datum and the entropy zero of the source.
- `close` condensed-phase records and transitions: Polymorph identity is in the name suffix; the flag's stepping rule and the multiple same-name records must be interpreted; transitions are implicit in adjacent record ranges.
- `narrower` reactant-only record: A temperature-independent assigned enthalpy is not a thermodynamic species model (no cp, no s); separating reactant-only species from products is a program role, not a property of the species.
- `unmapped` compiled thermo library (thermo.lib) and its derived fits: A mapping from thermo.inp that ignores the compile step represents ranges the solver never uses and omits an extrapolation it always applies.
- `close` trans.inp entry header: Binary entries are ordered in the file but physically symmetric; five pure entries carry names that match no thermo species; the reference is free text.
- `close` trans.inp coefficient rows: The property, its unit and the exponential are in code comments only; the Fortran exponent spelling with a space must be normalised at import.
- `unmapped` problem dataset: Calculation inputs belong to qualification and capability records, not the knowledge store.
- `unmapped` reactants, only, omit, insert and output datasets: Not knowledge.
- `close` legacy output tables: Legacy CEA2 results, not reproduced from the data in this tree; printed at limited precision (long mode gives 15 digits).
- `narrower` atomic data table: Valences used only for one derived quantity; the inert elements IH, IC, IO have no model counterpart.

### neqsim (44)

- `broader` COMP (table): One row mixes identity, conventions-dependent constants, parameters of many incompatible models and placeholders. A mapping must split it by consuming model, must drop template-filled cells rather than import them as data, and must carry the units (degrees Celsius, g/mol, bar) in a per-column conversion.
- `close` COMP_EXT (table): The file mixes real rows (257 non-GEN rows, largely copies of COMP) with generated rows whose parameters are placeholders. A faithful mapping loads identity and the varying constants only and records every template-filled cell as not_applicable or withheld; importing the template cells would assert water's parameters for 76 thousand species.
- `close` COMP columns: identity and bookkeeping: COMPTYPE mixes chemical class, phase behaviour role and model switches (ion, inert, HC); CAS placeholders and 4 mojibake names must not become identifiers; duplicate COMPINDEX values cannot be keys.
- `close` COMP columns: critical constants, acentric factor and basic state data: Celsius and bar must be converted at mapping time; ion rows and the default row carry template critical constants that are not physical data; MWAVG and PVMODEL are constants and carry nothing; LIQDENS and STDDENS have no stated unit or temperature.
- `close` COMP columns: ideal-gas heat capacity, formation data and sublimation: Polynomial in T with no stated range (nasa7 needs T_low and T_high); the NeqSim enthalpy zero (273.15 K sensible reference) differs from the formation datum and is switched by a runtime flag, so two energy_reference sets are needed; Cp polynomial coefficients are scaled by the gas constant 8.3144621 of this source, which the model requires as a slot.
- `close` COMP columns: liquid and solid density, liquid and solid heat capacity, heat of vaporisation: The form of LIQUIDDENSITYCOEFS and HEATOFVAPORIZATIONCOEFS is ambiguous because the code disagrees with the data; a mapping must choose one reading per column and record the other as a discrepancy. No units and no validity range are stated.
- `close` COMP columns: vapour-pressure, triple point and fusion: The form is selected by a text code plus a side condition on ANTOINEE, not by the code alone; units differ per type (bar, Pa-derived); the pow10 C shift is an implicit convention; no fit range is stated so envelope cannot be filled.
- `close` COMP columns: cubic-EOS alpha-function parameters: Columns are named after the form but the selection of the form lives in the assembly (attractive-term number); MCPR columns double as UMR-PRU coefficients with two implied zeros; hard-coded per-name overrides in code are not in the table and would be lost in a mapping of the table alone.
- `close` COMP columns: CPA and association parameters: Two parameter sets share one column for the association energy; the PR set is reachable only through the UMR-CPA component class; scheme codes need a site_scheme entity with site multiplicity and donor/acceptor charges that the table does not carry.
- `close` COMP columns: UMR-CPA parameters: Unit conversions are code-side, not in the table; a dependency on the UMR group-interaction tables (A_UMRMC etc.) is implied by the model but not recorded in the file.
- `close` COMP columns: PC-SAFT and SAFT-VR Mie parameters: Units of the segment diameter and the association energy are not stated; fallback chains (VR Mie to PC-SAFT) are code behaviour, not data, and would be lost if only the table were mapped.
- `close` COMP columns: electrolyte, dielectric and Henry parameters: The Henry form has a fixed additive constant ln 1.802 and no stated unit or solvent basis; ion-related code flags (K = 1e-40) are behaviour, not data.
- `close` COMP columns: hydrate and wax parameters: The Langmuir form A/T*exp(B/T) is an inference from the evaluator, units are not stated, and the reference fugacity basis is model code; two parameter sets coexist under different column names.
- `close` COMP columns: transport and surface-tension parameters: Type code plus four cells do not declare units; defaults (0.5, 0.7) are behaviour in code; template values must not be imported as data; LJ diameter doubles as an ionic diameter in code.
- `broader` INTER (table): One row holds thirty-odd parameters of incompatible models; model-specific keys (exact phase class) decide which columns are read, so the row has no model-independent meaning. Missing rows mean 'use zero' in the code and must become stateful absences or declared defaults, not stored zeros.
- `close` INTER columns: key: Keys are names, not identifiers, and 28 of them do not resolve to a COMP row.
- `close` INTER columns: cubic-EOS and PC-SAFT kij: The PR versus SRK column is selected by an exact Java class name, so a parameterization boundary exists that the file does not declare; the value 1 for ion pairs is a convention, not a fitted parameter; KIJTType -1 has no defined meaning.
- `close` INTER columns: CPA cross-association and CPA kij: Combining rule is a per-pair switch hidden in a data column with its meaning only in a comment; the oriented pair cpakijx/cpakjix and the symmetric cpakij coexist; cross association is defined per site pair in theory and here per component pair.
- `close` INTER columns: Huron-Vidal: The per-pair HVTYPE switch makes one mixture use two mixing rules; energy parameters have no stated unit; orientation is decided by string position in the row relative to the phase's component order.
- `close` INTER columns: Wong-Sandler and NRTL: Duplicate value families (HV versus NRTL) could be one set or two independent sets, the file does not say; KIJWS is a dead column.
- `close` INTER columns: electrolyte w-parameters and other model columns: Two of the seven columns (W2, W3) are zero in every row; the w switch chooses between a stored value and a built-in constants formula, so the stored W1 is meaningful only together with the code that computes the alternative; the viscosity parameter lives in a thermodynamic table.
- `close` UNIFACGroupParam (group table): Main-to-secondary grouping and the scheme revision (original, PSRK, UMR) are not declared; the same group table is reused for three schemes whose interaction matrices cover different main-group ranges (64 versus 70).
- `close` UNIFACcomp and UNIFACcompUMRPRU (component group assignments): The same component can have different assignments in the two tables and the file does not say which scheme revision each belongs to; the ragged row (CompNumber 135) and the unread columns must be skipped; the _PC rule is code.
- `close` UNIFAC interaction matrices (a, b, c; classic, UMR, UMR-MC): Selection between the UMR and UMR-MC tables is a rule on the alpha-function number of the first component, not a parameterization property; absent versus zero is not distinguished; a b/c matrix does not state its unit.
- `close` PitzerParameters: Units are not stated; the temperature form is documented in a code comment only; Tmin/Tmax are unread in NeqSim but are real applicability ranges; mixing parameters theta and psi are columns that hold no data.
- `unmapped` PHREEQC Pitzer catalogue (resource referenced, not in the pinned tree): The data file is not in the pinned bytes; only its loader and the constants describing it are.
- `close` REACTIONDATA family (reaction equilibrium-constant tables): Functional form, log base, pressure convention, the meaning of R, ACTENERGY and USEREACTION are not in the pinned bytes; three overlapping parameterizations share INDEX and NAME; apparent-constant tables (Kent-Eisenberg) are valid only together with their model.
- `close` STOCCOEFDATA (reaction stoichiometry): Participants are component names not species forms; aggregation and standard state are not stated; 4 stoichiometry indices have no equilibrium data and 12 equilibrium indices have no stoichiometry.
- `close` COMPSALT (salts as ion pairs): Only the ion split is used by the library; solubility coefficients have no stated form or unit.
- `close` MBWR32param (modified Benedict-Webb-Rubin coefficients): Equation terms are only in the Java code; units of the coefficients are not stated.
- `close` ISO6976 constants tables: Units and reference-state conventions per column are not stated; the consumer is outside the pinned tree.
- `close` AdsorptionParameters: Units and pressure basis are not stated; one row carries parameters of five models.
- `close` HenryWater sidecar (JSON, coverage CSV, BibTeX): The bridge from Hsbp at 298.15 K to HenryCoef1 is not stated; the sidecar is metadata about COMP, not a data source that the library reads.
- `close` GibbsReactDatabase (formation data and polynomial coefficients): Functional forms, units and temperature ranges are not stated; the file format (decimal comma) needs a dedicated reader.
- `unmapped` Process-support tables (pipe data, compatibility rules, scale remediation, fiscal and power-generation catalogues): Out of scope for thermodynamic knowledge.
- `close` TBP fraction (pseudo-component input and result): The same pseudo-component can carry critical constants from a user override (addTBPfraction_Mw_Sg_Crit) or from correlation, and only the code path tells them apart; the derivation has no declared model version; values depend on the EOS selected (m parameter, Peneloux constants) so a pseudo-component is not EOS independent.
- `close` Plus fraction and its carbon-number distribution: The split depends on an embedded molar-mass table with no stated source and on name parsing; a distribution parameter set (A, B, C, D) per fluid is not stored anywhere except in the model object.
- `close` Lumped pseudo-components and lumping result: Lumping is lossy and irreversible in the library (delumpResolution exists only for re-characterisation); the membership of a lump is recorded only by its name and boundaries.
- `close` Assay cut (refinery assay input): Basis (mass versus volume), the 60 F water density and the boiling-point midpoint convention are code-side conventions; the cuts for standard components mix component identity into an assay.
- `close` SARA and asphaltene characterisation inputs: Defaults are assumptions in code; SARA fractions are a composition basis not in the model's composition_basis list.
- `close` Characterization options and validation report: The operation is procedural; the transfer and de-lumping choices would have to be recorded as a derivation's method parameters.
- `close` Fluid exchange formats (JSON neqsim-fluid and Eclipse E300 reader): Units are fixed by convention; the volume-shift sign and the eos-name to model-assembly mapping are code-side.
- `close` Component name resolver tables (embedded in source): The synonym table is code, not a dataset; the ambiguity rule (missing entry means pass through) is behaviour.
- `close` Reference-equation and ion parameter tables embedded in Java source: The data are not separable from the code in the pinned tree; term structure must be recovered from array layouts; the EOS-CG class comment says its backend must be populated with the publication's parameters while the backend delegates to a model documented as GERG-2008-shaped (see discrepancy).

### phasepy (16)

- `broader` component: One object holds parameters of a dozen forms with no record of which parameterisation or publication each came from, so a mapping must split it into several parameter sets that share only a label. Identity is a free-text name. The SAFT fields have no consumer and map to nothing usable.
- `close` mixture: The mixture object fuses the component list, the model choice and the parameter values; none of the choices is recorded as data, and actmodelp aliasing means the active activity model is implicit.
- `close` quadratic mixing rule kij matrix: The same attribute name serves the symmetric and the asymmetric case; a mapping has to choose the transposition rule from a flag of the call, not from the data.
- `close` Wong-Sandler and SAFT kij matrices: The WS kij multiplies a combined (b - a/RT) term that depends on temperature, so its meaning is tied to the pure a and b of the chosen alpha function.
- `exact` NRTL interaction matrices: The g1 unit statement disagrees with the equation; a mapping must take the dimension from the equation.
- `narrower` ternary NRTL correction vector: A three-entity subject tuple with component-indexed slots does not fit a pair-keyed parameter set; the form is undocumented beyond the code.
- `close` Wilson interaction matrix: The Wilson parameter in this library is an energy in K with volumes drawn from a separate correlation; other libraries use the same name with dimensionless Lambda.
- `exact` UNIQUAC interaction matrices: The coordination number is a constant in code, not a slot.
- `exact` Redlich-Kister pair polynomials: Pair order carries a sign that only a parity transposition rule keyed by the polynomial order can express; the pair list is positional.
- `close` UNIFAC component group assignment (GC): The scheme is implicit in which workbook the model reads; a name that is duplicated in a workbook (CHO) cannot be assigned unambiguously.
- `exact` UNIFAC subgroup record (RkQk row): Duplicate subgroup names need the main group as a second key; the scheme (Dortmund 2018 or 2021, original) is carried only by the file name.
- `exact` UNIFAC main-group interaction cell (Dortmund A0, A1, A2): Missing pairs are an open-world gap that the source turns into a closed-world zero; the orientation of the matrix is implicit in code.
- `close` original UNIFAC main-group interaction matrix (A0 sheet): The row labelling defect (see discrepancy) means a mapping cannot trust the GroupID labels and must rebuild the row-to-main-group association from Sheet1.
- `unmapped` legacy unifac.xlsx tables: Unread, undocumented and of unknown variant; it would be a parameterisation of an unknown UNIFAC variant.
- `close` SGT influence parameter polynomial and beta matrix: The pair parameter lives on the EoS object and the pure polynomial on the component, so one parameterisation is split across two objects.
- `narrower` SAFT-VR-Mie corresponding-states coefficient tables: The output feeds no PhasePy model, so the estimated values have no consuming form in this source.

### phreeqc (31)

- `close` SOLUTION_MASTER_SPECIES: The model's basis/secondary role does not carry the valence-state element as its own conserved total with its own master species and its coupling through e-; the alkalinity contribution per master and the Alkalinity pseudo-element have no counterpart; atomic weights are per-database values with no edition named; the choice of master species (the basis) is part of the data and changes every reaction's K and every species' alk.
- `close` SOLUTION_SPECIES: Equation text is retained only as the reaction's equation; PHREEQC's rewriting of every species reaction to secondary master species means the stored K is relative to a chosen basis (changing the master species changes the numbers), which the model records only through system_member roles; per-species activity, transport and volume options belong to other model objects and do not share the reaction's record; the defined-species-first convention has no slot except system_reaction.defines.
- `close` log K temperature function (-log_k, -delta_h, -analytical_expression): The source stores both forms for one reaction and picks one by a silent non-zero test at load; the model would keep both as parameter sets and needs a selection rule (precedence analytic over van't Hoff) recorded as a convention; the equilibrium-constant reference pressure (1 atm) and R are hard-coded in the code, not in the data, so they must be supplied as convention_set values.
- `exact` delta_h units: The original unit is not needed after conversion; the mis-parse risk for unit tokens containing 'c' is a property of the reader, not of the data.
- `close` -gamma (WATEQ Debye-Hueckel ion parameters) and default activity coefficient: The implicit defaults (Davies for ions, 0.1 I for neutrals) are not data but code, so they must be recorded as a selection_policy rule; the same option name means different equations in EXCHANGE_SPECIES and with -llnl_gamma.
- `close` -llnl_gamma, -co2_llnl_gamma and -activity_water: Three different activity routes share one option family keyed by the species; the flag values are internal gflag integers with no data representation, and the ln(10) and 55.51 constants are fixed in code.
- `close` -dw (tracer diffusion and conductance parameters): a3 acts as a global mode switch when the H+ entry exceeds 24, so a per-species value carries phase-wide meaning; the water viscosity used as a reference is code, not data.
- `close` aqueous -Vm (molar volume): The volume form depends on water properties (density, dielectric constant, Born derivative) coded in PHREEQC; the model must name them as assumptions or reimplement them; whether the block is used depends on the presence of a global block in the same database.
- `close` -viscosity (Jones-Dole ion parameters): The code comment in transport.cpp writes exp(b2*tc) and exp(d2*tc) while the code and the database comments use the negative exponent (see discrepancy); the tenth value is carried but unread; the 25 C redefinition makes b0 and d1 derived values when positions 8 and 9 are given.
- `close` -millero (Millero density coefficients): The seventh value is carried by the parser but has no meaning in the calculation.
- `close` -erm_ddl, -no_check and -check, -mole_balance: The species composition in PHREEQC is sometimes not the name's formula (polysulfides, isotopologues), so the model must store the composition separately from the name.
- `close` -add_logk and -add_constant: The added vector adds into whichever representation the receiving reaction has after selection, so the dependency is additive over parameter vectors rather than a reference to a whole parameter_set.
- `close` PHASES: Gas versus solid is a property of how the phase is used in an input block, not of the database entry; the name-suffix rule for the formula and the silent replacement of (aq) and H2O(l) are reader behaviours; the phase and species namespaces are separate and case rules differ (phases case-insensitive, species case-sensitive).
- `close` EXCHANGE_MASTER_SPECIES: The site total is an input-block quantity; the model's site_class holds a site ratio per formula unit, not an amount of exchanger per solution.
- `close` EXCHANGE_SPECIES: The convention (Gaines-Thomas equivalent fractions, dummy activity of X-) is implicit in the code through gflag 4 and must be recorded as a standard_state on each participant; the -gamma option on an exchange species changes the exchange convention rather than describing the species' own activity coefficient.
- `close` SURFACE_MASTER_SPECIES: The three psi masters per site label are created implicitly and are electrostatic unknowns rather than chemical species; the model has no concept of a potential unknown, so they are noted as dropped.
- `broader` SURFACE_SPECIES: Electrostatic potential, capacitance and diffuse-layer choices live in the SURFACE input block and in unknown potentials; the data alone (log K plus dz) cannot be evaluated without that choice, so the model must hold the model choice with the parameter set.
- `close` PITZER block (options and flags): Species tuples are stored as a set keyed by type, so repeated species in a tuple lose their multiplicity and unordered handling is implied for every type; the automatic E-theta terms and the alpha defaults are code rules the data do not contain; the MacInnes, redox and etheta flags are model choices that belong to the assembly, not to parameter sets.
- `close` Pitzer parameter row (B0 B1 B2 C0 THETA LAMBDA ZETA PSI ETA MU ALPHAS APHI): Keying by a set loses the multiplicity of a repeated species in a tuple, which matters for MU (n,n,n') and LAMBDA (n,n); roles (cation, anion, neutral) are derived from charges, not stored; the alpha values and ETHETA are not in the rows; the temperature function has six terms here but only five in SIT.
- `close` SIT block (-epsilon, -epsilon1, -epsilon2): Unlike Pitzer, every row in the data uses a single constant; the five-term temperature function and the epsilon1/epsilon2 forms are accepted by the code but unexercised; species-charge roles are not stored.
- `close` LLNL_AQUEOUS_MODEL_PARAMETERS: The block's side effect of disabling water-property calculations is a global behaviour that no parameter slot captures; the grid is linear-interpolated with a hard stop outside, which is a tabulated_function interpolation rule plus an envelope.
- `close` NAMED_EXPRESSIONS (also NAMED_ANALYTICAL_EXPRESSIONS, NAMED_LOG_K): The entry is not attached to a reaction, so it is not a parameter_set on a subject in the model's sense; the ln_alpha1000 scaling is applied on read.
- `close` ISOTOPES, ISOTOPE_RATIOS, ISOTOPE_ALPHAS: The isotopic ratio programs are BASIC code in CALCULATE_VALUES; only their names and targets are data.
- `unmapped` CALCULATE_VALUES: Behaviour lives in a procedural BASIC program; any mapping keeps only the text.
- `unmapped` RATES: The rate law is code; the meaning of each PARM position lives in comments; the coupling to KINETICS input (-parms, -m0, -formula) is outside the database.
- `close` RATE_PARAMETERS_PK, RATE_PARAMETERS_SVD, RATE_PARAMETERS_HERMANSKA: Column meanings are in comments; the equation is BASIC code inside the interpreter (RATE_PK etc.), so the table cannot be evaluated without that code.
- `unmapped` MEAN_GAMMAS: A derived-quantity definition with no parameters; it has no slot in the knowledge model.
- `narrower` GAS_BINARY_PARAMETERS: The pair is keyed by phase names rather than species identities and each pair is stored twice; the hard-coded defaults live in code.
- `unmapped` Input-level keywords found in database files (END, PRINT, DATABASE, SOLUTION, EQUILIBRIUM_PHASES, REACTION) and INCLUDE$: Control keywords carry no thermodynamic meaning; the selection effect of END on which blocks a database contains is recorded under selection.
- `narrower` SOLID_SOLUTIONS (input block, not present in any database file): Several of the options specify a0 and a1 indirectly (gaps, critical point) so the stored parameters must be solved at the parameter temperature; ternary and higher non-ideality is not representable.
- `unmapped` Simulation-input keywords (no database data): SOLUTION, EXCHANGE, SURFACE, EQUILIBRIUM_PHASES, GAS_PHASE, KINETICS, REACTION and related: Not data; the keyword names are recorded so the set of accepted blocks is complete.

### polykin (13)

- `close` Tait parameter row: The subject is a code name with no repeat-unit or molar-mass information; C is a constant outside the table; units live in a docstring.
- `close` polymer component description in PolymerACM (DP, F, s): DP is a property of a sample, not of the polymer type; the molar-mass distribution is collapsed to a single number. Positional roles instead of typed entities.
- `close` Flory-Huggins chi matrices: The composition basis is not recorded, so it has to be supplied by the parameterisation; the size vector m is an input of the evaluation, not of the parameter set.
- `close` NRTL matrices (Aspen form): The same letters mean different terms in different classes of one package; the parameter slots are coefficient families of a temperature function rather than values.
- `close` UNIQUAC parameters: Matrix letters a to d are temperature-function coefficients, not direct tau values.
- `close` Wilson parameters: The Wilson name covers two different parameterisations across sources; the form must be distinguished by slot meaning.
- `exact` property equation instance: Units and base are instance fields rather than slot types.
- `close` Vrentas-Duda parameter set: Mixes a diffusivity parameter set with an embedded thermodynamic chi; the chi depends on the basis (mass fraction of solvent) used to fit it.
- `close` kinetic coefficient instance (Arrhenius, Eyring) and chain-length-dependent coefficient: No reaction identity or stoichiometry is attached to a coefficient; the reaction framework in kinetics/reaction.py is not importable (see discrepancy).
- `close` copolymerization model parameters: Penultimate models need a triple of monomer states (radical penultimate, terminal, monomer) that a pair subject cannot express without an index family.
- `close` copolymerization dataset (MayoDataset, DriftDataset, kpDataset): The copolymer composition basis (molar, by repeating unit) is implicit.
- `close` molecular-weight distribution objects: The distribution object carries its weighting kinds as methods, not as separate records; the repeating-unit molar mass M0 is a single number.
- `narrower` reaction species and reaction system (unexported framework): The module is not imported by the package and cannot be imported as written, so the intended semantics are read from class bodies only.

### pycalphad (24)

- `close` ELEMENT: H298-H0 and S298 are a datum for the element in its reference phase and have no slot in the energy_reference model unless modelled as element_reference values; the reference phase is a bare name that may match no declared PHASE; the atomic-mass edition is not stated; a zero cannot be told from not given.
- `exact` SPECIES: The reader upper-cases names and keeps a fractional stoichiometry as float; associates are ordinary species with multi-element formulas.
- `close` FUNCTION: The model has no free-standing named function: a FUNCTION is a shared nested set referenced by several parameters, so the mapping needs a dependency relation per reference and a value type for 'expression with symbolic references'; temperature limits read literally (zero outside) and as used by Model (extrapolated) differ; the expression grammar (LN, EXP, **) needs the expressions page of the declaration.
- `broader` TYPE_DEFINITION: One statement carries three unrelated meanings (magnetic model constants, order-disorder pairing, never-disorder flag) plus an ignored family; order-disorder pairing is a relation between two phase definitions that the model has no native relation for, and the 'never disorder' switch changes the equation.
- `close` PHASE: Aggregation is not a field of PHASE (the L/G/A hints are optional letters, not a required attribute); a phase option is a model selection and belongs to the model assembly rather than the phase definition; the sublattice-count integer is redundant.
- `close` CONSTITUENT: The major-constituent flag is dropped at parse time and so cannot be mapped; the source order of species is not retained.
- `broader` PARAMETER (syntax): The 'order' integer means three different things by arity; the source ordering convention (alphabetical) is not stated in the file and is imposed by the reader; the reference key is lost at read time; the wildcard '*' stands for every species of a sublattice and is not a constituent array; diffusing species is an extra subject role only for kinetic types.
- `close` PARAMETER G and L (Gibbs energy and excess): G versus L are two letters for one fact in the source; the order meaning and the auto-expansion of ternary order 0 are behaviours of the evaluator and not of the stored numbers.
- `close` PARAMETER TC, NT and BMAGN (magnetic): The sign convention (negative means antiferromagnetic, divided by the afm factor) is an evaluator behaviour that must be carried as a declared convention; the afm and structure factors live on the phase (TYPE_DEFINITION) and not on the parameter.
- `close` PARAMETER GD and THETA (two-state and Einstein): THETA stores a log of a temperature: a slot type for 'natural log of a temperature' is needed or a declared transform.
- `close` PARAMETER V0, VA, VC, VK (molar volume): VK and VC are listed by the parser but no code evaluates them; the standard pressure is a constant of the evaluator.
- `unmapped` PARAMETER VISC, ELRS, THCD, SIGM, XI, MQ, MF, DQ, DF, VS (property and mobility types): Content that the source stores but never evaluates; any mapping would be untested by the source and needs a transport or kinetics form.
- `unmapped` DEFINE_SYSTEM_DEFAULT: The meaning is given only by Thermo-Calc's manual, which is not in the pinned tree.
- `unmapped` DEFAULT_COMMAND: Interpretation (vacancy and electron gas are system defaults) is inferred from the writer, not stated.
- `narrower` DATABASE_INFO: The text is not read by pycalphad, so any use of it comes from the raw file.
- `close` ASSESSED_SYSTEMS: Only free text; the model has no structured coverage list.
- `close` LIST_OF_REFERENCES: The parameter-to-reference linkage exists only in the raw text; after pycalphad's read it cannot be recovered.
- `unmapped` skipped and unsupported keywords: TEMPERATURE_LIMITS carries per-system limits that are dropped; a file using TABLE, CASE or COMPOUND_PHASE cannot be read at all.
- `broader` Database object model: A Database merges a chemical system, a parameterisation and a partial convention set (mass only) into one object with no revision, no provenance and no rights fields.
- `close` ChemSage DAT header: Datum and gas constant of the export are not in the file; the ChemApp documentation the code cites is not in the pinned tree.
- `close` DAT endmember (Gibbs energy equation block): Equation types not supported by the reader are not represented; additional-term exponent 99 is a code for ln(T).
- `broader` DAT solution phase models read by pycalphad (IDMX, RKMP and RKMPM, QKTO, SUBL and SUBLM, SUBG, SUBQ): Each code selects a whole equation family and parameter layout; 12 floats per SUBQ excess line are not interpreted by the source; the QKTO exponent offset is a parsing convention.
- `close` DAT stoichiometric compound block: The compound becomes a multi-sublattice phase with one element per sublattice; the species identity is the compound.
- `unmapped` DAT chemical group override string: Read and warned about but not evaluated, and the model has no per-subsystem interpolation selector.

### pygaps (13)

- `close` isotherm header (BaseIsotherm): The model's adsorbed_amount observables fix a per-host-mass basis and mol/kg; a volume, fraction, percent or per-mole material basis has no observable and needs molar mass, density or both; the adsorption kind (absolute or excess) cannot be recorded and the observable must be chosen by assumption or left unmapped; defaulted units can silently attach the wrong unit; a material is only a name.
- `close` PointIsotherm data: The model's branch is an enum per point, which matches; uncertainty kind would be not_stated; extra columns need an observable each (an enthalpy column needs a declared observable), else they are carried as unmapped.
- `close` ModelIsotherm: The model's forms are not in the catalogue yet; the parameter units depend on the data units and need conversion; rmse is normalised by range, not a model-form quantity; temperature is part of the subject, so a parameter set is valid at one temperature only.
- `close` Material record: Identity is by name only, with no registry key, structure, batch or texture; density has no declared model quantity for a bulk material.
- `close` Adsorbate record: Cross-sectional area, kinetic diameter, polarizability and quadrupole moment have no observable in the starting set; unit strings such as 10e18 esu cm are not pint-parsable as written; p_critical in bar conflicts with the model's Pa storage unit and needs conversion.
- `close` adsorbate property type: Units are text, not quantity types.
- `close` JSON isotherm file (pyGAPS): As for the isotherm header.
- `narrower` NIST ISODB JSON reader mapping: pyGAPS handles only single-component isotherms with a two-part unit string and absolute pressure; excess versus absolute is retained only as opaque text; wt% is mishandled by a factor 100 by the stated reading.
- `close` AIF file: Per-point p0 has no dataset column concept except as another property column; the operator tag is a person, not an attribution.
- `close` CSV and Excel isotherm files: Units are stated both in the unit keys and in the column header names; the two can disagree.
- `close` unit and basis tables: STP is defined only through the numerical factor; the amu entry is not a mass relative to grams in the way the other entries are.
- `unmapped` Horvath-Kawazoe material property sets: No model concept for pore-size-method material parameters; values are uncited.
- `close` DFT kernel and standard isotherm tables: The kernel is a two-axis table and needs one tabulated function per pore width or a new kind; its origin is not stated.

### pyprism (9)

- `close` System (site types and kT): Site types are not species: several site types belong to one molecule through omega, and one site type can be shared across molecules; molecule identity and connectivity have no place in the model.
- `unmapped` site density: The basis is a site number density in reduced units; the model has mole, mass, volume, segment and surface fractions but no per-volume site density.
- `close` site diameter and contact distance: A diameter and its combining rule are not separate records in the model; a hard core is tied to it.
- `close` pair tables (potential, closure, omega): The table holds code objects, not values; the objects carry the parameters (epsilon, sigma, omega form).
- `close` pair potential object: No combining rules and no units; potentials are attached to site-type pairs, not to species.
- `close` intramolecular correlation function object: Architecture (linear, ring, grafted, block) exists only as the choice of function and its length; connectivity between distinct site types is not a record.
- `unmapped` Domain (radial real and Fourier grids): A numerical grid is solver state, not thermodynamic knowledge.
- `close` closure object: The closure is a per-pair choice inside one solve, not a parameter of a species.
- `close` reference correlation tables (data files): The model has no observables for correlation functions in k or r and no structure-factor quantity types.

### reaktoro (12)

- `close` database document: The file carries no identity, version, convention or provenance statement; the parameterisation and system have to be named by the loader from the file name.
- `close` species record: Formula plus Charge plus Elements is stored redundantly; no structure identifiers, so identity resolution has to work from the formula, charge and aggregate state; the species Name carries the aggregate suffix in some databases and not in others.
- `exact` StandardThermoModel block: none for the named parameters; the single-model-per-species rule means alternatives from different compilations are separate databases, not alternative parameter sets of one species.
- `close` FormationReaction block: The reaction is the definition of the species and is not a free-standing reaction; reactants are species identified by name within one file; the direction sign is the opposite of ThermoFun's (reactant positive here).
- `close` Pitzer parameter file: The temperature correction is itself a choice among 11 forms selected by a name string, which the model expresses as a nested set accepting a contract; triples are unordered among cations or anions and need a permutation-group transposition.
- `close` Extended UNIQUAC parameter file: Four layouts of the same content; the T-dependence coefficient count differs by version; the model forms differ by the pressure term uP (only in v2023).
- `close` Palandri-Kharaka parameter file: Mechanism keys carry catalyst identity inside the key text (a(H+)); aliases are identity assertions; the rate needs a reaction and a surface area model from elsewhere.
- `exact` cubic EoS parameter file: none, but the file is unread: the constants are hard-coded in Support/CubicEOS.cpp, so the file is documentation that can drift from the code.
- `close` PHREEQC keyword blocks as Reaktoro consumes them: Everything the extraction does not copy (rates, isotopes, exchange and surface behaviour, Pitzer and SIT parameters of the .dat) is lost; parameters reach Reaktoro only as closures over PHREEQC structures, not as data.
- `close` NASA CEA species as converted (nasa-cea): A species with intervals of different aggregate states (condensed phases melting within the fit range) is one species here but several species forms in the model; the state is per interval.
- `close` SUPCRT linearized line and the legacy XML species: The XML and the Dissociation, acentric factor and temperature-range blocks that the JSON drops are data not carried into the current format.
- `close` built-in element, critical-property and dissociation tables: atomic-weight edition is not stated; critical data are for selected pure substances, matched by alias names.

### rmg_database (34)

- `close` database file framing (entry / tree / file-level variables): The file-level free text is unstructured; the solvent variable is a convention of the whole library and needs a parameterization attribute that the model does not declare (convention_set has no solvent slot); an executed script cannot be treated as data by the pipeline, so a parser must reproduce the loader's binding rules.
- `broader` entry() of a thermo group tree: Precise: the None state is not a missing datum but an instruction (fall to the nearest ancestor with data in group, radical and pair files; average the children in ring and polycyclic files), so the model must carry that rule on the estimation derivation, not on the node; a pointer has no declared target scheme (labels are scanned within the same file) and chains of pointers exist; the pattern language is retained verbatim and nothing in the model can match it.
- `broader` group node data states (data object, pointer string, None): value_state has no state for 'use the nearest ancestor' or 'use the average of the children'; both are procedures of the estimator and differ by file, so a mapping has to attach the file's rule to the group_scheme or to the derivation; mutation of the averaged value back onto the node at run time is not data and must not be imported.
- `close` entry() of a thermo library: The adjacency list is a structure notation with no declared naming scheme (naming_scheme has no entry for it) and its canonical key needs a graph canonicalisation that the model does not specify; spin multiplicity is part of identity here but not an attribute of species; metal and facet have no attribute (material.registry_key is free text); rank and referenceType cannot be mapped without a declared vocabulary; ThermoData has no declared form.
- `close` adjacency list (molecule): No declared structure scheme; charge and multiplicity live in the text and must be lifted into species.charge and composition; resonance forms of one species appear as separate molecules in different places; explicit hydrogens versus implicit hydrogens in group patterns.
- `close` adjacency list (group pattern): Retained verbatim; nothing in the model can evaluate it, compare two patterns or decide which is more specific, yet the tree position and estimator correctness depend on those relations, so the structural parent relation must be imported from tree() instead of inferred from patterns.
- `close` logic node group definition (OR{...}): The model has no union relation between groups; the components are separate groups and the union must be represented by pattern text or an extra relation that does not exist.
- `narrower` tree() hierarchy text: The model's group.parent carries no ordering among siblings, but matching picks the first matching sibling by position; order must be kept as an integer attribute or the tree matcher would be non-deterministic on overlapping siblings. Repeated tree labels (5 in radical.py) need the load order.
- `close` ThermoData: No declared form for a discrete Cp table with H298 and S298 and piecewise-linear integration; uncertainty per Cp point needs one slot_uncertainty row per index; the mixed units are converted per value.
- `exact` NASA and NASAPolynomial: Unit of the coefficients is not stated in the file; Cp0, CpInf and E0 have no slot in nasa7; Tmin and Tmax of the object duplicate the pieces' limits.
- `unmapped` Wilhoit: No Wilhoit form is declared; the form must be added to the catalogue before import.
- `broader` quantity tuple and uncertainty syntax: slot_uncertainty needs an uncertainty_kind and coverage; the source states neither coverage nor distribution, so the mapping must declare an unspecified-coverage kind; a multiplicative factor on A is relative on a log scale, which the magnitude column cannot express without a declared kind.
- `close` thermo group file roles: The model's group_scheme_role has no value for a radical (HBI) increment or for a pair interaction; additive_increment is the nearest. The order of application and the centre type (atom, pair, ring) belong to the estimation derivation, which has no attribute for them.
- `close` SIDT node (subgraph-isomorphic decision tree): The 9-vector has no declared form; the trained tree's training data are not in the tree; uncertainty meaning is not stated.
- `unmapped` thermo uncertainty data (covariance of group values): The model says joint covariance belongs to the fit, but fit has no attribute or relation for a covariance matrix over parameter sets, so this evidence has no home; the quantity the matrix refers to is not stated in the files.
- `close` reference and referenceType: Plain-string references have no DOI or year and need parsing; referenceType values are not one vocabulary and map to origin_role only by guess (Theory to computed, experiment to measured, review to evaluated, estimate to estimated, uncategorized to none).
- `broader` kinetics family definition (groups.py header): The model has no construct for a reaction class with an action recipe; the recipe is an executable transformation over labelled atoms and has no representation as parameters; template and products consistency is checked only by the loader.
- `close` entry() of a kinetics family group tree: Patterns are multi-centre (labelled atoms '*1' to '*6') while group has one pattern text and no centre structure; tree roots correspond to reactant slots and need a slot index.
- `unmapped` forbidden structure patterns: Exclusion constraints on mechanism generation are not thermodynamic knowledge and the model has no construct for them.
- `close` entry() of a kinetics rate rule (rules.py): The subject is a tuple of tree nodes with one node per reactant slot, each in its own scheme, which the slot-group subject roles can express only if group is a declared kind per slot; the enthalpy-dependent activation energy has no declared form; rank has no vocabulary.
- `close` entry() of a training reaction and its dictionary: Reaction identity from a label plus dictionary needs species resolution through the adjacency lists; species are not joined across dictionaries; degeneracy is a rate convention with no attribute; atom labels are reaction-local.
- `close` entry() of a kinetics library (reactions.py and dictionary.txt): Collider species and efficiency dictionaries need a slot shape the model does not declare (efficiencies map species to factors); the merge of duplicates into one object at load time is behaviour, not data.
- `close` Arrhenius, ArrheniusEP and ArrheniusBM rate objects: No rate-law forms are declared; the rate unit depends on reaction order, which the model expresses only through a quantity expression per form; EP and BM need a dependency on the reaction enthalpy at 298 K.
- `close` pressure-dependent and falloff rate objects: Efficiencies are a map from species to factor, which has no slot shape; nested sets of a form that implements a rate contract are supported by the model but no such contract exists; the reduced-variable definition of Chebyshev needs the range slots as data.
- `close` surface and charge-transfer rate objects: Coverage dependence is a species-keyed nested dictionary, charge transfer needs a potential as an operating variable, and Marcus needs temperature-dependent inner-sphere terms; none is in the model.
- `unmapped` KineticsModel with solute transition-state data: Reaction-level solvation corrections for transition states (difference descriptors) have no construct; a mapping would need a solute-descriptor slot group with reaction subjects.
- `close` RateUncertainty: An uncertainty of ln k at a reference temperature is not an uncertainty of a slot; it cannot be split into A, n and Ea.
- `close` kinetics family sets and recommended libraries: The auto-selection rule (elements present, temperature threshold, PAH keyword) is code in auto_database.py and cannot be stored as data; a policy records only the order.
- `close` SoluteData, SolventData and DataCount objects: The solvent and the solute are roles in one equation (pair-like subject) with no declared form; standard state and units are unstated; V is computed in one place and stored in another.
- `close` TransportData and CriticalPointGroupContribution: Epsilon unit varies (energy or temperature) and needs the gas constant to convert; Joback contributions have no declared unit or form.
- `unmapped` GroupFrequencies and Conformer (statmech): Statistical-mechanics mode lists are a model description, not parameters of a declared form; frequency ranges are estimator inputs, not measured values.
- `close` binding energies of metals (surface library): Facet has no attribute of material; the reference of the energy (gas-phase atom) is inferred.
- `unmapped` quantum-chemistry correction dictionaries: Corrections are a method applied to quantum output, not thermodynamic data of species; they belong to a computation derivation, which the model records only as lineage.
- `close` ReferenceSpecies (reference sets): Only H298; the level-of-theory key strings must be parsed; geometry has no construct.

### rmg_py (17)

- `close` Entry and Database (loaded records and tree): A node's data can be a string or None with estimator-specific meaning; the model's value_state covers the string (redirect) but not the None instruction.
- `close` Molecule, Atom and Bond: Resonance forms belong to one species but are separate graphs; spin multiplicity has no attribute of species; surface site and morphology have no counterpart.
- `close` Group, GroupAtom and GroupBond (pattern objects): The matching semantics (atom-type hierarchy, list wildcards, labelled-atom mapping) cannot be stored; only the text can.
- `unmapped` AtomType vocabulary: A structural vocabulary with a hierarchy and action tables; the model holds patterns as text and has no construct for the vocabulary they draw on.
- `close` LogicOr and LogicAnd: No union relation between groups.
- `close` Species: Bookkeeping attributes of a run (index, creation_iteration) have no meaning in the model.
- `close` Reaction, TemplateReaction, LibraryReaction and DepositoryReaction: Flags that steer the generator (allow_pdep_route, elementary_high_p, allow_max_rate_violation) are not knowledge.
- `broader` KineticsFamily and ReactionRecipe: The recipe is an algorithm over labelled atoms, and the generation of products from reactants is not data the model stores.
- `broader` estimate comment strings: The comment carries the group list, weights and repeats only as text; importing the estimate's lineage means parsing the grammar; uncertainty of the estimate is not recorded anywhere in the object (add_thermo_data adds values only).
- `close` ScalarQuantity, ArrayQuantity and UnitType factories: Unit strings follow the quantities package, not pint; conversions must be revalidated; the coverage of the uncertainty is not stated.
- `close` physical constants module: No edition statement exists and the Hartree energy has two values in the trees; a convention_set must pin R = 8.314472 for this source.
- `close` HeatCapacityModel base attributes and E0: Cp0 and CpInf of a record are estimates from structure when missing; E0 has no counterpart.
- `close` SoluteData, SolventData, SolvationCorrection and KfactorParameters: K-factor and Henry-constant relations use CoolProp saturation densities and pressures (an external source) and have no counterpart.
- `unmapped` Conformer and statmech modes: A structural model rather than parameters of a declared form; symmetry numbers and optical isomers enter entropy here but the group-additivity thermo handles symmetry separately and has no optical-isomer term.
- `close` TransportData and CriticalPoint: The Neufeld integral coefficients are in code.
- `unmapped` LevelOfTheory and CompositeLevelOfTheory: The model has no structured computation-method record.
- `close` rank to accuracy map: A conversion from an ordinal to a numerical uncertainty, unlike any measured uncertainty.

### sgte_unary (10)

- `close` file header and change log: The change log is free text; a mapping cannot turn it into supersedes relations or per-parameter revisions.
- `close` ELEMENT (reference phase, mass, H298-H0, S298): Zero H298-H0 and S298 cannot be told from not given; the reference phase name is a bare string that is not in the set of declared phases for 4 elements (see discrepancies); the datum of the energy is implicit.
- `exact` SPECIES and the GAS phase: none for the species; the gas parameters have no pressure dependence (no ln P or standard pressure is stated).
- `close` PHASE and CONSTITUENT: The ratios 1:3 (BCC) and 1:0.5 (HCP) describe interstitial sites in the source convention; the prototype names are in the phase names only (A1, A2, A3 and so on), not in a field.
- `close` FUNCTION GHSER (element energy relative to SER): The datum (H at 298.15 K of the reference phase set to zero) is not stated by the file, only implied by convention and the function name.
- `close` FUNCTION lattice stability (G<phase code><element>): The link from a lattice-stability function to the GHSER function is a symbol reference inside the expression, which a mapping must turn into a dependency.
- `close` PARAMETER G (unary endmember energy): The order index is 0 for all; the comment-borne source citations are not attached to any parameter in a parsed file.
- `close` PARAMETER TC and BM/BMAGN (magnetic): The sign convention of TC and BM and the factors on the TYPE_DEFINITION lines have no statement in the file; the abbreviation BM versus BMAGN is a spelling difference.
- `close` TYPE_DEFINITION: The meaning of the type character I in 'I&' and similar is not stated in the file.
- `unmapped` DEFINE_SYSTEM_DEFAULT and DEFAULT_COMMAND: Directive text with no model target.

### sigma_profiles_pyscf (6)

- `broader` sigma profile row (main Parquet): Axis unit e/A^2 differs from the model's C/m^2 storage unit and needs conversion; the three hydrogen-bonding blocks need three slots or an enum-indexed family (no declared role); float32 values carry rounding the text files did not have; the entity is a CID-keyed computation, so identity resolution to a species depends on the index's structure notation; area and volume are redundant with the profile sum; generation settings (averaging, geometry, theory level) belong to a derivation and convention, not to row values.
- `close` sigma profile index row: Several CIDs share one InChIKey (19,948 keys) and therefore one species with different geometries and different profiles (sampled 2,000 shared keys: median relative area spread 0.065 percent, 95th percentile 1.5 percent, maximum 10.1 percent; same SMILES in 1,995 of the groups); a canonical species therefore has several competing profiles, which the source does not rank. Chemical_Family is a rule output, not an identity; empty strings must not be loaded as assertions.
- `close` sequential refit parameters: The fit's training evidence is not included, so the derivation input list is empty; RMSE values have no slot (the fit record has objective and outcome only); the hard-coded baseline RMSEs are not computed in the script; no covariance exists to store.
- `unmapped` integrity results: The claim that all profiles round-trip is an assertion by the producer that cannot be rechecked here because the source text files are not acquired.
- `unmapped` cavity radii table and cavity settings: No model concept for quantum-chemistry settings; carried as derivation method text.
- `exact` rights and citation statement: The clause that the data terms include a paper that is not yet citable has no model slot.

### surfpack (7)

- `close` component set (ThermoPack identifier string): Identity and parameters are delegated to another source, so SurfPack alone holds neither.
- `unmapped` weighted-density weight set: The model has no construct for a weight function; functional structure lives outside a pointwise expression (docs/expressions.md, structure_declared_equation_external).
- `unmapped` density profile (Profile) and grid: The model describes homogeneous phases; an inhomogeneous density field has no place in it beyond a tabulated function.
- `unmapped` external potential: Wall-fluid interactions belong to adsorption on a host, which the model covers only through the adsorbent entity; these potentials are functions of position.
- `unmapped` solver specification: Solver tuning is procedural knowledge, not data.
- `close` planar LJ-spline MD profile row: Units and method are not stated; the dataset concept needs them.
- `close` LJTS critical and surface tension table: No units, no source and an unlabelled duplicate row.

### teqp (24)

- `close` model specification document ({kind, model, validate}): Parameters are embedded in the assembly document rather than referenced as records with provenance; units live in key strings; a document can contain a whole mixture's parameters (kmat, coeffs), which are parameter sets that a mapping must separate from the assembly.
- `unmapped` JSON Schema documents of the model kinds: The schemas are the only machine-readable statement of the specification language and they are narrower than the code in places (see questions), so they cannot be taken as the contract without checking the factory.
- `close` multifluid model specification (kind multifluid): Identifier-based parameter lookup, file-path indirection and the estimate fallback are selection-policy behaviour embedded in the loader; flags are free-form; the R rule is an assembly choice.
- `exact` kinds vdW1 and vdW: none beyond units.
- `close` kinds PR, SRK and cubic (generalised cubic with alpha functions): The alpha function is chosen per component with a type tag inside an array aligned to component order; the PR78 alpha exists only in code; the gas constant default is a silent choice.
- `close` kinds QCPRAasen and RKPRCismondi2005: The temperature-dependent covolume and the volume translation are extra terms that exceed a plain cubic form; units of As and Bs are implied.
- `close` kind advancedPRaEres (PR with excess-energy mixing rule): The restriction to binary mixtures and the Wilson-only factory are code behaviours that a form declaration would not capture.
- `close` kind CPA (cubic plus association): Two association specifications coexist (legacy class versus sites); the schema accepts only the legacy one.
- `close` kinds PCSAFT and PCSAFTPureGrossSadowski2001: The universal constants are a parameterization choice stored as a flag; polar terms switch on by presence of a pair of numbers; the library of three fluids is a tiny embedded dataset.
- `close` kind SAFT-VR-Mie (with polar models and flags): Units are chosen per key in an alternative-keys scheme (sigma_m or sigma_Angstrom; mu_Cm or mu_D); the polar model is a combination of three independent choices (term, J integral, K integral) encoded in a string.
- `close` kinds SoftSAFT and genericSAFT, and the association model specification: Site labels are free text without a declared scheme and multiplicity comes from repetition; radial_dist handling is ambiguous in code.
- `close` kinds GERG2004resid, GERG2008resid, GERG2004idealgas, GERG2008idealgas: The separation of residual and ideal gas into two models means a consumer must combine them; the recomputed n0 differ from the stored published constants.
- `close` kind LKP: The kmat convention differs across kinds under one key name, so a pair slot must carry its combining convention.
- `close` kinds multifluid-ECS-HuberEly1994, multifluid-association and multifluid-activity: Wrappers nest whole model objects inside model objects; the conformal transformation is a procedure on a reference model; the change of gas-constant rule inside a composition is easy to miss.
- `close` activity residual models (Wilson, binaryInvariant, COSMO-SAC-2010): The two Wilson specifications differ in how volumes arrive; sigma profiles are tabulated functions with no interpolation rule stated.
- `close` kinds AmmoniaWaterTillnerRoth and LJ126 (no-argument kinds): Parameters inside source code cannot be separated from the model without transcription; dimensionless LJ units need a unit-system convention in the model.
- `close` kinds SW_EspindolaHeredia2009, EXP6_Kataoka1992, Mie_Pohl2023, Mie_Chaparro2023 and the 2CLJF family: Dimensionless simulation units need a unit-system record; a neural network is a parameter set of 6435 numbers with no physical slot meaning.
- `close` kind IdealHelmholtz and its term types: The same ideal-gas function has two parameterisations with different numeric coefficients (scaled by Tc and rhoc), so two carriers of one published set differ by a scoped transformation that uses the reducing state.
- `close` multifluid mutant (Python-level model built from a multifluid model): It is a run-time transformation of a model object rather than a stored assembly; the pair slot groups show all three transposition behaviours (symmetric gamma and phi, reciprocal beta, parity lambda).
- `narrower` fluid file (CoolProp format) and accepted residual term types: Two carriers of the same equation (CoolProp and teqp copies) differ in 27 of 124 files and teqp has dropped the superancillary blocks, so the source file alone does not identify which equation version it carries.
- `close` binary pair record and departure function record (teqp copies): Duplicate pairs with different values (R1234yf with R134a; CO2 with R1234yf; CO2 with R1234ze(E)) are two parameter sets for one subject that a file position resolves; the function reference by name without alias support differs from CoolProp's alias resolution.
- `close` REFPROP fluid and mixture files (FLD and HMX.BNC): The parsers are in a vendored third-party library not surveyed here; the survey records only that teqp accepts the formats.
- `exact` GERG-2004 and GERG-2008 parameter tables (GERG.hpp): Two parameterizations share rows by fallthrough (GERG-2008 falls back to GERG-2004 for unchanged pairs), a supersession relation that has to be made explicit per subject.
- `close` embedded numerical tables of the SAFT, association, FeANN and cubic models: Global constants of a model form belong to the form's parameterization with its own provenance; the PC-SAFT constants here duplicate those in FeOS (feos.toml) at lower precision (10 digits against 14); the neural-network weights have no physical slots.

### thermo (34)

- `close` InteractionParameterDB table (metadata plus data): The file stores a default for absent pairs as if it were data; a model must keep absence as absent (no row) and record the default as a policy. The T dependent flag names no equation, so the equation each table's coefficients belong to has to come from code or docstrings (see the per-table constructs).
- `narrower` ChemSep PR kij row: The Tmax bound and the exact window text exist only in the unread .ipd comments; pressure units of Pmin, Pmax and P are stated nowhere in the JSON.
- `narrower` ChemSep NRTL row: alphaij ranges from 0.0 to 9.1633 across rows, far outside the usual 0.2 to 0.47 window, and is stored per orientation although equal; bij is half of a tau whose other terms are not represented; the unit conversion from cal/mol is applied before storage and not recorded.
- `narrower` ChemSep Wilson row: aij is not an independent parameter but a function of two pure-component volumes; storing it per orientation duplicates information and ties the row to one volume table.
- `narrower` ChemSep UNIQUAC row: The pair parameters cannot be evaluated without pure-component r and q that live in a different (unextracted) place; the default of 0 is not neutral in UNIQUAC.
- `narrower` Henry pair row (A to F): Units and basis (Pa versus a solubility form, mole-fraction versus molality) are not in the data; a structural-zero coefficient cannot be separated from a fitted zero; the PRTranslated E = 1.0 has no stated meaning.
- `close` EPPR78 predicted kij row: A cache of a model evaluated at one temperature would have to be regenerated from the group assignments and PPR78 group-pair parameters, not stored as data; the extreme values (-19.8) signal fragmentation outside the method's validity.
- `broader` ChemSep IPD text row: Carries windows, pages and duplicate-pair history that the JSON drops; nothing reads it, so any model that uses it must parse it itself.
- `close` ScalarParameterDB table (metadata plus data): As for the interaction tables: defaults stored as if data; the name field duplicates the key and carries no compound name.
- `narrower` Twu alpha row (PRTwu_*, SRKTwu_*): The fit assumed one specific EOS and volume translation (dependency consistent_with); the tables do not say which critical constants they were fitted with.
- `narrower` Volume-translation row (PRVolumeTranslation_*, SRKVolumeTranslation_*): Duplication of the same fitted number under PRc and TwuPRc must be collapsed to one set with two uses, or the dependency kept.
- `narrower` API-SRK row (chemsep_APISRK): The version string on the table disagrees with the version of the XML the values were read from (8.26 versus 8.32).
- `narrower` Mathias-Copeman row (chemsep_PSRK_matthias_copeman): The polynomial variable of the library form is not recorded alongside the table; a mapping must fix it from the code or the original publication.
- `narrower` Regular-solution row (chemsep_regular_solution): The reference temperature is absent; the stored numbers are conversions of the source units.
- `narrower` UNIFAC interaction row, one parameter (UFIP, UF2IP, LLEUFIP): The 0 default for absent pairs is indistinguishable from a stored zero; the 10000.0 value looks like a sentinel for 'no data' but is stated nowhere; the revision of the DDBST table is not recorded.
- `narrower` UNIFAC interaction row, three parameters: Two functional forms share one file shape; the form must come from the scheme and version, not from the columns. Absent pairs, stored zeros and the diagonal are conflated; late VTPR files silently overwrite earlier ones on 12 keys in the loader.
- `narrower` UNIFAC interaction row with validity range (NIST 2015): If the envelope is not modelled the library's dropping of the interval is reproduced; if modelled, it adds information the source code ignores.
- `broader` UNIFAC_subgroup record: The record mixes thermodynamic parameters (R, Q) with cheminformatics patterns (SMARTS, atoms, bonds, priority) that are not thermodynamic knowledge; subgroup ids cannot be used as identifiers across schemes.
- `narrower` UNIFAC main-group map entry (UFMG, DOUFMG, VTPRMG, PSRKMG, LLEMG, LUFMG, NISTUFMG, NISTKTUFMG): Redundant with the subgroup records; where they disagree (NISTUFMG) the subgroup records are what the loader uses.
- `narrower` DDBST compound group-assignment row: The partial decompositions stored under flag 0 have no place unless modelled as rejected assignments; the TSV is keyed by InChIKey while the library's lookup path is keyed by CAS integer through an artefact not in the tree.
- `narrower` Fitted equation-parameter leaf (Misc correlations): Derived-from-data fits without their data: the evidence cannot be rebuilt; Tmin and Tmax for some leaves equal Tc or a single point (coolprop leaves have Tmax = Tc).
- `close` Fitted polynomial leaf (stable polynomial, exp polynomial, ln-tau, JANAF, UNARY): Fits of other libraries' models: the knowledge is in the source model, the polynomial is a lossy carrier with its own error; the pycalphad leaves fit a heat capacity with very large high-order coefficients (largest magnitude 1.29e12), reproducing values only within the fit interval.
- `narrower` Redlich-Kister mixture leaf: Needs the parity transposition rule and a nested-set coefficient; the property is surface tension, an excess observable not a Gibbs energy.
- `close` T-dependent correlation model registry (correlation_models): Equation bodies live outside this tree; only names and parameter lists are available here.
- `unmapped` Regulatory inventory rows (Law): Regulatory status is outside the thermodynamic domain model.
- `narrower` PPR78 and EPPR78 group tables: Absent pairs coincide with zero; the predicted kij depends on T, Tc, Pc and omega, so it is a derivation not a stored parameter.
- `narrower` Joback and Diky-Joback group tables: Units are implied; the method is an estimator whose outputs are estimates of pure properties.
- `narrower` Wilson-Jasperson, Bondi and Fedors increments: Estimator tables only; outputs are estimates.
- `unmapped` Functional-group SMARTS library: Cheminformatics patterns, not thermodynamic knowledge.
- `close` Grayson-Streed and Chao-Seader coefficient sets: No source is recorded for the coefficients, so provenance must be marked not established.
- `broader` ChemicalConstantsPackage: A resolved, source-mixed result container with no per-value provenance; it is the output of selection, not data.
- `broader` PropertyCorrelationsPackage: It is a runtime binding of selected methods.
- `narrower` Bell 2018 Twu table row: Critical constants here duplicate constants held elsewhere; the file sits under Phase Change and is read only by a test.
- `broader` ChemSep XML compound record (dev): A richer source than anything thermo extracts; the library ignores UMR and most equation-numbered data.

### thermochimica (13)

- `close` DAT header block: Datum, gas constant and atomic-weight edition of the export are not in the file.
- `close` Gibbs-energy equation block (species or compound): Interval selection (upper-inclusive, upward extrapolation) differs from the TDB convention and must be a declared rule; the gas correction constant 0.10945 is a code behaviour; dummy species are a numerical device, not chemistry.
- `exact` IDMX block (ideal mixture): The treatment of the first phase as a gas with pressure dependence is an assumption in the code, not a field.
- `broader` QKTO block (quasichemical Kohler-Toop): Interpolation overrides are a per-triad choice with no slot in the model; the equivalent-fraction conversion factor is a phase property.
- `close` RKMP and RKMPM block (Redlich-Kister-Muggianu polynomial): Terms index species of the phase by position in the list, so the subject is an ordered tuple of species with the file order significant for odd orders.
- `broader` SUBL and SUBLM block (compound energy formalism): The solver variables are endmember mole fractions, not independent site fractions, so a phase with fewer endmembers than site-fraction degrees of freedom is a reduced description; the model's site-fraction basis is a different composition coordinate.
- `broader` SUBG and SUBQ block (modified quasichemical, quadruplet): Two-sublattice pair-and-quadruplet bookkeeping and 12 uninterpreted numbers per excess term have no slot; the parser's species replacement (pairs to quadruplets) means the file's species are not the solver's species.
- `broader` SUBI block (two-sublattice ionic liquid): The case classification is a code construct over charges; the model must carry the ionic site-ratio rule and per-case interaction forms.
- `broader` SUBM block (two-sublattice ionic, no neutrals or vacancies): Author-stated as equivalent to SUBI without neutrals and vacancies; the equivalence is by code comment only.
- `narrower` Thermochimica input script: Conditions are scripts, not stored relations.
- `close` stoichiometric (pure condensed) phase entries: The label text after the name is dropped; polymorph identity is encoded only in the name.
- `close` magnetic terms: The two phase-level numbers are named differently in the two readers (afm and structure factor in pycalphad, structure factor and p in Thermochimica's comment) and the correspondence is inferred.
- `unmapped` interpolation override line: The model has no per-subsystem interpolation selector.

### thermofun (13)

- `close` thermodataset file header: A dataset is at once a parameterisation (a published set meant to be used together), a chemical system (its species list) and an implicit convention set (water triple-point reference); the file states only the label, so a mapping has to create the convention set and the system from the dataset name and from engine defaults.
- `close` element record: The entropy and mass are attached to the element here but belong to an energy reference and an atomic-weight edition in the model; the record says neither, so both must be inferred from the dataset.
- `broader` substance record: The record is one species form plus its standard-state parameter sets for several forms at once (Cp polynomial, volume, HKF, Landau, EoS) plus reference values that are properties of the model's reference point, not parameters; a mapping has to split the list into parameter sets by method, turn reference properties into slots of the heat-capacity form, and decide the standard state, concentration scale and solvent that the record does not state. Zero errors mean 'no error stated' in some cases and a true zero in none that can be told apart.
- `close` property block (values, units, errors): The model forbids uncertainty as a slot and requires a kind for it; here a zero error stands for 'unknown'. The status field that would carry calculated-versus-read provenance is never read and appears only in fixtures.
- `broader` TPMethods entry: A list that is at once an assembly of independent slot fillers (Cp base, volume, transition, solvent) and a bag of alternatives cannot be told apart without the code-to-slot table in C++; the model's assembly needs the slot, which the JSON holds only implicitly in the numeric code. The code-to-name pairs are stored as {code: name} and the two can disagree (trailing space in a name).
- `close` method code vocabularies: The vocabulary is the form catalogue of ThermoFun; several entries are combinations (water equation of state plus triple-point convention) rather than a single equation.
- `close` class_ and aggregate_state codes: The pair (class, aggregate state) mixes state of matter with standard-state and calculation role; a mapping to aggregation drops the class, which is what carries solvent and solute roles.
- `close` cp_ft_equation parameter blocks (m_heat_capacity_ft_coeffs, m_phase_trans_props): The model's family with an interval per piece fits the intervals; the transition block is a per-boundary row with its own slots, not a slot of a piece; the model has no 'interval continuity with jump' declaration, so the transition increments need a separate nested family. The T^0.5 coefficient is labelled with a J/(mol*K^1.5) unit and multiplied by T^0 in the Cp formula of the code (see discrepancy).
- `exact` eos_hkf_coeffs: none for the seven named parameters; the extra value and the unit mismatch need a rule.
- `close` eos_akinfiev_diamond_coeffs, m_landau_phase_trans_props, eos_gas_crit_props: Unlabelled values need their meaning from the code; 7-slot arrays share one block name across EoS families, so the form cannot be read from the block name alone.
- `close` reaction record: Stoichiometry and the reference values map directly; the method list mixes a logK(T) form, an extrapolation marker and a volume marker in one list, and the reference values are sets of slots of the logK form. The link from the reaction to the substance it defines is stored on the substance (field reaction) and implied by equal symbols on the reaction.
- `close` reaction parameter blocks (logk_ft_coeffs, dr_heat_capacity_ft_coeffs, dr_ryzhenko_coeffs, dr_marshall_franck_coeffs, dr_volume_fpt_coeffs, dr_dolejs_manning10_coeffs): The blocks are unnamed in the files; the coefficient meaning lives in the reader. Extrapolation markers (logk_3_term_extrap) carry no block: the 12-value block sits on the logk_fpt_function entry, so the marker and the coefficients are in different entries.
- `exact` reaction-defined substance: none in structure; the model's 'defines' column on system_reaction and the dependency relation carry it, but the file does not assign a chemical system or a basis (the master species are implied by which substances have methods).

### thermohub (11)

- `close` document key and identity convention: The same species from several source databases is several vertices with no explicit identity link; any identity resolution is left to the loader. Code-label enums differ between snapshots, so codes cannot be loaded without the snapshot.
- `broader` substance vertex: As for the ThermoFun substance record; in addition the source database, concentration scale and Debye-Hueckel parameters are extra attributes that the model places on the parameterisation, the standard state and a model assembly respectively; unit-free mass_per_mole must be given a unit by assumption.
- `close` reaction vertex: Stoichiometry sits on edges, not on the vertex, and the equation text repeats it; the law-of-mass-action datasets define every species by a reaction, so a mapping must treat those reactions as the standard-state parameter sets of the species rather than as independent reactions.
- `close` reaction method blocks new to ThermoHub: Coefficient naming differs from the ThermoFun layout (A1..A5 here, A0..A6 there) and the unit statements are absent, so term identity is inferred.
- `close` nasa_polynomial method entries: The model's nasa7 family is exact for the 9-value blocks; the other lengths need a separate form or are dropped; aggregate state is AS_OTHER so the state of each interval has to come from elsewhere.
- `broader` element vertex: conserved_quantity covers the decoupled-nitrogen case; reference-form entropy belongs on an energy reference.
- `close` thermodataset vertex and reactionset vertex: A dataset is at once a parameterisation, a system and a convention set; TDS_LMA versus TDS_GEM distinguishes two parameterisation styles (standard-state properties versus equilibrium constants) that the model expresses through different forms.
- `exact` datasource vertex: none for bibliographic fields; DOIs are nearly absent, so identity of the publication is by short name.
- `close` graph edges of the substance-reaction-dataset graph: The master and defines relations map to the model's system_member role and system_reaction.defines; citing with a field path needs a per-slot attribution that the model records at the record level.
- `close` phase vertex, component edge and mixing model: Interaction parameters are unstructured text and their slot names are sometimes blank; the phase's internal structure (sublattices) is absent, so every phase is structure none; Ncomps and the substances list disagree with the edges.
- `close` SIT interaction vertex and its edges: The pair is an unordered relation carried by two edges; the model's symmetric slot group takes it directly, but the species order in the key text is arbitrary and the unit of epsilon is not recorded.

### thermoml_schema (76)

- `broader` DataReport (root) and Version: A DataReport mixes a publication, a compound table, samples and datasets; a mapping splits it. The version statement has no home other than the carrier pin.
- `close` Citation (CitationType) and TRCRefID: Keywords, abstract, language, source status, TRCRefID and the book, journal and thesis specifics have no attribute in publication; authors have no list attribute; eType is a ten-value vocabulary the model does not declare.
- `close` Compound and RegNum: CAS numbers arrive as integers and must be re-rendered with hyphen and check digit before they match an identity scheme; the polymer averages are point statistics (number, mass, viscosity, peak, Z average), not distributions, and the viscosity and peak averages have no weighting member in the model (weighting has number, mass and area); mixture_definition has by_definition and by_measurement but the substance types alloy, clathrate, complex, crystal and solution have no attribute; eSpeciationState (mixture in equilibrium of species versus a single species) has no facet; biomaterial identifiers (EC number, PDB id) have no naming_scheme.
- `close` Sample (purity and purification): Purity in percent must be divided by 100; nUnknownPerCent maps to purity_basis not_stated; the stepwise purification history, the water and halide impurity contents, several purity values per sample and the analytical method have no attribute; sample source and status enumerations have no attribute (supplier is free text).
- `close` PureOrMixtureData: dataset_kind (measured, evaluated, computed, verification) is not a field: it has to be read from the Property method choice (CriticalEvaluation gives evaluated, Prediction gives computed, eMethodName or sMethodName give measured or derived). component_function has component, solvent, solute, adsorbent, adsorbate and catalyst, so AuxiliarySubstance functions Buffer, Inert and Cofactor have no member. The dataset title is absent in the schema.
- `close` Property (element of PureOrMixtureData) and Property-MethodID: The model has no slot for ePresentation or eRefStateType as data on a column: the reference-dependent quantities must become distinct observables (relation facet) and ratios and temperature differences need observable identities the facets cannot express (see the mapping of ePresentation and eRefStateType).
